decision.msg: Question: how does Servex avoid trying to start a second copy of a worktree's already-running server when the proxy hits it mid-restart? Options considered: (a) leave runner()/autostart() as-is, since a registered project has no Process in this.processes so autostart would call runner(name) -> build a fresh Process and spawn node server.js in the worktree dir on the SAME port it's already bound to, throwing EADDRINUSE noise into the log every time the proxy has a hiccup; (b) add project.external=true, set on Project by the new POST route, and check it in both Project.start_command() (returns null) and Servex.runner() (treats it like project.self - never spawns). Chose (b): a registered project is something Servex ROUTES to, never something it MANAGES - the same boundary self already draws for Servex's own dashboard. Rule: code#2 (a module is a class; every method is a seam) - extending the existing self-guard by one clause was smaller than adding a parallel check.
decision.alt: leave autostart free to try spawning a duplicate process on the registered port

decision.msg: Question: where do worktree-up.mjs/worktree-down.mjs find Servex's dashboard port? Servex.js itself reads process.env.SERVEX_PORT with a default of 8090 (readme.md confirms 8090 is the documented default). Matched that exactly in both scripts rather than inventing a second env var name, so one override (SERVEX_PORT) moves both Servex and every script that talks to it.

assign.outcome: **A worktree can now register itself with Servex and the proxy reaches it — proven end to end, and `npm ci` no longer hangs on Windows.** Two routes on `Servex.js`, loopback-only like every route: `POST /api/projects {name, path, port?}` adds a project to the list and the proxy's port map (pinning the given port, or allocating one from the registry), and `DELETE /api/projects/:name` removes it from both — each logs one `project` event. A registered project is marked `external: true` so Servex only ever ROUTES to it, never tries to spawn a second copy of a server it didn't start. `worktree-up.mjs` calls the POST after its server boots, `worktree-down.mjs` calls the DELETE at teardown; both stay completely silent and succeed when Servex isn't running — a worktree still works with Servex off. The `npm ci` Windows bug (`spawnSync EINVAL`, Node's CVE-2024-27980 .cmd guard) is fixed with `shell: true`. Proof, one real run: `node Server/worktree-up.mjs routes-proof` finished unattended in 5954ms (was throwing before; npm ci itself took 736ms for 70 packages) and registered itself — `curl -H "Host: routes-proof.localhost" http://127.0.0.1:8080/framework/` returned 200 through the live proxy, and it appeared in `GET /api/projects` (= `list_servers`) with `external: true, can_start: false`. `node Server/worktree-down.mjs routes-proof` ran in 1467ms and afterward the same proxy request 404'd, the project was gone from the list, and the worktree, its branch and `.worktrees.json` were all gone from disk. `Servex/readme.md` got the "Surviving a reboot" section with the exact `schtasks` line (written, not run) plus a line on the new routes in the Port registry paragraph. Left for the owner: running that one `schtasks` line — a login-time task is the owner's own machine config, not mine to set.
